findings: One-story curve is too sparse and non-monotonic to locate a breakpoint: 96.0% at 1 QPC, 93.3% at 24, 94.4% at 178. The 2.7pp dip at 24 may be noise, packing/order artifact, or a local minimum, not a proven scale-up cliff.
178 QPC is only story-validated, not module-stack-validated. No size above 1 QPC should be treated as a recommended operating point until it survives a full stack.

Repeatability and quality can diverge. Test-retest can stay high while exact-quote copy, polarity consistency, or agreement vs 1-QPC gold fall first. Score those as separate failure modes on the same outputs.
Call cost is inverse to QPC. Full 1-QPC restory is the expensive arm; coarse screens should use already-observed 24 and 178, then spend 1-QPC only on stratified subsamples and failed quote items.

A full factorial over QPC x stories x stacks x polarity x quote-type is unnecessary. Adaptive bracket-and-bisect on the first failing story, then transfer only last-good and first-bad, minimizes total calls.
recommendations: Pre-register degradation now: drop vs 1-QPC baseline of >=2.0pp on test-retest, >=3.0pp vs 1-QPC gold, exact-quote fail rate doubling, or mixed-vs-blocked polarity gap >=3pp. Require 95% CIs and paired same-item scoring. Do not declare 24 or 178 good or bad from the current 3-point story.

Wave 0, Stack A only, reuse Story 1 labels. If raw traces exist, rescore exact-quote span match and polarity by batch slot before any new calls. That is zero-call evidence on whether 24 failed on quotes, order, or homogeneous polarity.

Wave 1, stack completion before any new QPC. On remaining Stack A stories, two independent repeats at only the already-run sizes 24 and 178. Skip full 1-QPC. Add a 24-item 1-QPC gold subsample per story, stratified by polarity and quote-need. Stack-validate 178 only if every story stays inside the thresholds; otherwise 178 must not be recommended.

Wave 2, breakpoint refinement on the first failing story only. If 24 is uniquely worst, bisect 16 then 20 (or 32 if 24 was noise and 178 failed). If 178 fails and 24 holds, probe 48 then 96 on that story, never jumping an untested size. Two repeats per candidate. Stop when last-good and first-bad differ by <=8 QPC.

Wave 3, within-stack transfer of only {1-QPC subsample, last-good, first-bad}. Do not rerun the coarse grid. Last-good for Stack A is the minimum last-good across its stories. That value is the only size eligible to recommend for Stack A.

Wave 4, module-stack transfer. On Stack B, start at min(Stack A last-good, 24), two repeats, one story. If it holds, step up only through sizes already validated on Stack A. If it fails, search downward through those same sizes. Never test or recommend a QPC on B that A has not already passed.

Wave 5, polarity mixing and exact-quote, nested not factorial. At last-good and at 24 on Story 1: one blocked-polarity batching and one shuffled mix. Score exact-quote items separately on those outputs. Spend extra 1-QPC calls only on quote items that failed at last-good.

Operating rule after the hunt: recommended QPC = min last-good that survived all tested stories on at least one full module stack and then transferred to a second stack. Until a second stack passes, recommend no higher than the 1-QPC-validated regime plus the smallest stack-validated last-good, and never above 178. Target about 80-150 judge calls total by early-stopping and by avoiding 1-QPC full restories.
risks: Treating 94.4% at 178 as clearance for 178-wide batching will violate the stack-validation rule and can hide earlier cliffs on other stories.
Adaptive search on Story 1 can overfit; a local 24 dip may vanish on story 2, wasting refinement calls or locking a too-small cap.
1-QPC subsample gold can miss rare exact-quote failures and understate quality loss.
Blocked vs mixed polarity and item order are confounders; if Wave 1 reruns 24/178 with a new shuffle, results will not be comparable to the original 93.3%/94.4%.
Position effects inside a batch (first/last k items) can look like a QPC effect if not sliced by slot.
Small n on one story makes 96.0 vs 93.3 vs 94.4 compatible with noise; without CIs the hunt may chase a non-effect.
If Stack B degrades earlier than A, the transferable cap may be far below 24; recommending A's last-good globally would overstate robustness.
output.summary: Existing 1/24/178 agreement on one story cannot locate a QPC breakpoint and does not validate any operating batch above 1 QPC. Run a gated progressive hunt: finish Stack A at only 24 and 178, bisect on the first failing story, transfer last-good then first-bad across stories and stacks, and nest polarity plus exact-quote scoring. Recommend only a size that has passed at least one full module stack and never anything larger than that validated cap.
